_what: the dependency gradient: what each room says, and at which rung
_note: DERIVED from commons/data/depth_rulings.json (authored). Do not edit.
_rule: Explain a dependency when ignorance of it prevents the learner from forming the intended mental model. Do not explain it merely because it exists.
_thrownness: The learner arrives late. There is no point at which they have arrived early enough to hold all the prerequisites — that is the condition of learning, not a defect to be repaired. So the question is never 'what must be taught before this?' (there is always one more) but 'what must become visible now for the next action to be intelligible?'

ladder.gloss: in the building, never on the path
ladder.shows: nowhere — the basement. Listed once in the book, so the museum is honest about having one, and never on a wall.
ladder.why: The museum should be allowed to have a basement full of explanations the visitor never visits. That does not make it dishonest; it makes it navigable.

ladder.gloss: the learner acts through it and need not know it exists
ladder.why: THIS IS THE DEFAULT, and the default is silence. A child meets sentences containing words they do not know without every unknown word becoming a prerequisite. The code is allowed to be more sophisticated than the learner's current vocabulary.

ladder.gloss: it has a name here, one line, no theory
ladder.shows: a plaque line beside the thing
ladder.why: Naming is not teaching. 'This is the instruction that makes a point appear' is a name; 'here we define a function whose parameter has type Vector3' is a lesson nobody asked for.

ladder.gloss: a small optional inscription says what KIND of thing it is
ladder.shows: the plaque line, plus a descent the learner may decline
ladder.why: Enough to stop it being magic. Not so much that the learner is asked to carry the abstraction yet.

ladder.gloss: the room teaches it; it is the room's subject
ladder.shows: the entrance board, and the room itself
ladder.why: What the learner needs in order to act. The museum can put these in their hands.

ladder.shows: nowhere — not a property of any one room
ladder.why: A fact about a learner's path, which no single room can know.

says.say: Three directions. They name where, not what.
Three numbers describe where something is.
Where the thing is, as against what it is.
You can see a sphere. What is there is three numbers. The visible thing is scaffolding for the invisible one.
The computer chooses the nearest allowed position.
says.descend: round() is one way a program asks for the nearest whole number.

says.say: The ball knows when your hand is inside it.
says.note: Later. Glimpse only — the grab works whether or not this is understood.

says.say: The thing that makes it visible.
A ball, standing in for a point that has no size.

basement.note: Museum infrastructure. It is why you have hands.
Deep background. It is why you can see.

says.say: One point was a position. Two are a relation, and a relation can be written down.
A single number. It has no direction and no parts, and it is not the line.
Two points determine an infinite line. Keeping only what lies between them is already a decision.
Give the segment an order — from here to there — and it points. Normalise it and only the pointing is left.
You measure by pulling. The hand is inside the instrument.
says.descend: The same gesture at one scale reads a length, and at another changes the thing it is reading. Nothing in the gesture tells you which you are doing.

says.say: A line you can aim is a line that can be aimed at something.
says.descend: It is the same object as the measuring beam. Pointing and destroying differ in what is at the far end, not in the line.

says.say: The line you measured with, two seconds later, with a mass on the end.
says.descend: Nothing was added to it but a body. It has to be swung: resting it against something does nothing, because the damage is not in the object.

says.say: The computer walks the same instruction along the line.
says.descend: A `for` loop repeats an instruction a fixed number of times — once per step of the walk.

says.say: Lines that agree never to meet, and the two that everything else is squared against.
Parallels that meet after all, because you are standing somewhere.
One man's body, turned into everybody's measure.
